claims.claim: DOSA is the first study of reverse-complement symmetry across multiple k-mer orders or taxa.

closest_prior_art.citation: Baisnee, Hampson and Baldi (2002), Why are complementary DNA strands symmetric?
closest_prior_art.overlap: Quantified complementary-strand symmetry for orders 1 through 9 across broad biological groups.

closest_prior_art.citation: Shporer et al. (2016), Inversion symmetry of DNA k-mer counts: validity and deviations
closest_prior_art.overlap: Quantified reverse-complement k-mer imbalance and its k-limit across chromosomes and species.

claims.falsifier: Already falsified as a novelty claim by the cited prior art.

claims.claim: DOSA is the first local or windowed analysis of reverse-complement word symmetry.

closest_prior_art.citation: Bastos et al. (2016), The exceptional genomic word symmetry along DNA sequences
closest_prior_art.overlap: Performed local sliding-window analyses of exceptional word symmetry with structural controls.

closest_prior_art.citation: Shporer et al. (2016), Inversion symmetry of DNA k-mer counts: validity and deviations
closest_prior_art.overlap: Used non-overlapping chromosomal windows when analyzing inversion-symmetry statistics.

claims.falsifier: Already falsified as a novelty claim by published local and non-overlapping-window analyses.

claims.claim: DOSA is the first genomic study to distinguish reversal from reverse-complement symmetry.

closest_prior_art.citation: Kong et al. (2009), Inverse symmetry in complete genomes and whole-genome inverse duplication
closest_prior_art.overlap: Compared reverse, complement and reverse-complement symmetries globally and locally over 786 chromosomes.

closest_prior_art.citation: Shporer et al. (2016), Inversion symmetry of DNA k-mer counts: validity and deviations
closest_prior_art.overlap: Explicitly contrasted inverse pairs with reverse, complement and random k-mer pairings.

claims.falsifier: Already falsified at the broad operator-comparison level by the cited studies.

claims.claim: DOSA invents exact dinucleotide-preserving sequence randomization.

closest_prior_art.citation: Altschul and Erickson (1985), Significance of nucleotide sequence alignments
closest_prior_art.overlap: Introduced random sequence permutation preserving dinucleotide usage.

closest_prior_art.citation: Jiang et al. (2008), uShuffle: A useful tool for shuffling biological sequences while preserving the k-let counts
closest_prior_art.overlap: Implemented uniform exact k-let-preserving shuffling using Eulerian-walk machinery.

claims.falsifier: Already falsified as an algorithm-invention claim by exact dinucleotide and k-let shuffling prior art.

claims.claim: DOSA is the first genomic resource to bind reference versions, checksums and computational provenance.

closest_prior_art.citation: NCBI Datasets genome processing and version status policy
closest_prior_art.overlap: Defines accession-version and assembly update semantics for reference genome resources.

closest_prior_art.citation: Wilkinson et al. (2016), The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship
closest_prior_art.overlap: Established reusable provenance and identifier principles for scientific data resources.

claims.falsifier: Already falsified as a general provenance-first claim by reference versioning and FAIR data practice.

claims.claim: A joint, representation-aware operator profile reveals residual biological structure that is not explained by exact dinucleotide composition alone.

closest_prior_art.citation: Kong et al. (2009), Inverse symmetry in complete genomes and whole-genome inverse duplication
closest_prior_art.overlap: Provides the closest broad comparison of reverse, complement and reverse-complement genome symmetries.

closest_prior_art.citation: Fariselli et al. (2021), DNA sequence symmetries from randomness: the origin of Chargaff's second parity rule
closest_prior_art.overlap: Provides a strong randomness and maximum-entropy explanation that any claimed residual must beat.

closest_prior_art.citation: Bastos et al. (2016), The exceptional genomic word symmetry along DNA sequences
closest_prior_art.overlap: Provides the closest local symmetry analysis under simple structural controls.

claims.distinguishing_feature: DOSA jointly separates positional R and RC distances, compositional R and RC k-mer orbit imbalance, circular origin/strand equivalence and periodicity, then calibrates the same windows against an exact dinucleotide-preserving null.
required_evidence: Freeze the pilot cohort and every parameter before examining outcomes.
Run the canonical Sounio producer with the exact dinucleotide primary null and publish exclusions.
Independently recompute the release-scope sample in Julia with the declared exact tolerances.
Quantify incremental information beyond GC, length, complexity, taxonomy and dinucleotide-null summaries.
Report effect sizes, uncertainty, multiplicity control, negative controls and sensitivity analyses.
Demonstrate out-of-sample or held-out-cohort stability of any retained residual pattern.
claims.falsifier: The claim fails if the joint profile adds no stable out-of-sample information beyond preregistered covariates and the exact dinucleotide null, or if an earlier study is found to implement the same complete design.

claims.claim: Replication-relative coordinate or replicon class has a reproducible association with residual operator profiles after preregistered controls.

closest_prior_art.citation: Shporer et al. (2016), Inversion symmetry of DNA k-mer counts: validity and deviations
closest_prior_art.overlap: Shows chromosome-wide and species-dependent deviations and documents known plasmid exceptions.

closest_prior_art.citation: Kong et al. (2009), Inverse symmetry in complete genomes and whole-genome inverse duplication
closest_prior_art.overlap: Connects inverse symmetry to genome-scale inversion mechanisms and local patterns.

claims.distinguishing_feature: The target is not a generic chromosome-plasmid difference: it is a preregistered effect on residual, operator-resolved profiles after exact dinucleotide null calibration and covariate control.
required_evidence: Predeclare origin annotation quality, coordinate transform, covariates and exclusion policy.
Use taxonomy-aware and assembly-aware held-out evaluation rather than treating windows as independent replicates.
Report chromosome and plasmid results separately with matched or modeled length, GC and sampling multiplicity.
Replicate the direction and practically meaningful effect size in a held-out expansion cohort.
claims.falsifier: The claim fails if the association disappears after grouped validation, exact-null calibration or preregistered covariate control, reverses in the held-out cohort, or is driven by a few assemblies.

claims.claim: DOSA can contribute a reusable operator-resolved complete-replicon atlas even if no new universal biological law survives testing.

closest_prior_art.citation: Baisnee, Hampson and Baldi (2002), Why are complementary DNA strands symmetric?
closest_prior_art.overlap: Supplies broad multi-order comparative analyses but not DOSA's proposed versioned per-window product contract.

closest_prior_art.citation: Kong et al. (2009), Inverse symmetry in complete genomes and whole-genome inverse duplication
closest_prior_art.overlap: Supplies a large complete-genome survey against which atlas scope and utility must be compared.

claims.distinguishing_feature: The proposed resource exposes decomposed operator metrics, topology and representation domain, exact-null summaries, ambiguity and exclusion records, accession versions, input hashes and executable receipts at window and replicon levels.
required_evidence: Release the frozen pilot and expansion manifests with accession versions and checksum closure.
Publish all canonical products, exclusions, schemas, parameters and validated run receipts.
Provide a stable DOI, license, data dictionary and documented example reuse analysis.
Compare coverage and field-level utility against the nearest existing datasets.
claims.falsifier: The contribution fails if the released resource is not materially more reusable or auditable than existing outputs, cannot be independently regenerated, or remains limited to engineering fixtures.

claims.claim: The current fixtures establish a dual-implementation scientific contract with Sounio as canonical producer and Julia as independent validator.
claims.distinguishing_feature: Persisted Sounio artifacts are independently recomputed by Julia with exact equality at the declared fixture scope; accelerators do not replace either authority.
required_evidence: Extend independent Julia recomputation from deterministic samples to the full release-scope chromosome products.
Bind both implementations, inputs, parameters and outputs into the pilot release receipt.
claims.falsifier: This engineering claim fails outside its stated scope if either implementation is absent, if any required mismatch occurs, or if accelerator output becomes an unvalidated source of scientific authority.
